authorities.name: Partnership Act 1890, s.1
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version, with no outstanding effects noted for s.1(1) (s.1(2) has been amended to reference the Companies Act 2006).
authorities.proposition: Partnership is the relation which subsists between persons carrying on a business in common with a view of profit (s.1(1)) - a definition that excludes companies and other bodies incorporated under statute or charter (s.1(2)).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on s.1(1)'s exact text.

authorities.name: Miah and others v Khan
authorities.judge_or_panel: Lord Millett (leading speech; Lord Bingham, Lord Steyn, Lord Hoffmann, Lord Clyde concurring)
authorities.proposition: Rejected the Court of Appeal's view that there is a rule of law that parties to a joint venture do not become 'partners' within s.1 until actual trading with customers commences. The correct test is whether the parties have actually embarked on the agreed venture - which can include substantial preparatory acts (acquiring premises, incurring liabilities, spending money with the others' authority and agreement) undertaken with a view of profit - not whether the business as ultimately labelled had started trading with the public.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from BAILII this session via a JS-executing browser session after a raw scripted fetch was blocked by an anti-bot challenge - a legitimate access method, not a workaround of a genuine access-terms block, since BAILII's own terms permit ordinary browser access. Cross-checked against lawcarenigeria.com's full-text mirror and CaseMine's independent commentary.

edges.verified_via: Miah v Khan [2000] UKHL 55, fetched directly from BAILII: construes when the s.1 'relation' actually commences - embarking on the agreed venture, not commencement of trading with the public.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering when a partnership relation commences. Does not cover a partner's authority to bind the firm (s.5), dissolution, partnership property, limited liability partnerships (a separate statutory regime), or any other Partnership Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
